title: Protocol for Preparing and Characterizing Samples for EPR Spectroscopy
author: Wort, Hett, et al.
materials: The following section describes MHQ sample preparation for the MloK1 CNBD and cAMP model system but can be extended to other protein-ligand pairs. It addresses: (i) the handling of both components for optimal ease-of-use during the MHQ sample acquisition, (ii) preparation and operation of the MHQ device, and (iii) packing and annealing of the sample in the EPR tube. At the end of this section, the sample is ready to be measured by PELDOR.1.Centrifuge approximately 200 μL of CNBD solution (300 μM stock) and 500 μL of cAMP (30 mM stock) at 13,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C. Store samples on ice until use.Optional: To reduce aggregation and improve the deuteration efficiency of the sample matrix, add deuterated ethylene glycol (20% (v/v)) to both protein and ligand solutions.Note: This prolongs the electron-spin phase-memory time TM and facilitates access to longer dipolar evolution times and, therefore, enables measurement of longer distances in PELDOR.22 However, note that cryoprotectants can alter structural equilibria, affect populations of conformational species,3,23,24 and increase the viscosity of the sample, potentially raising HPLC pump pressures. Always test cryoprotectant effects on the biomolecule’s stability and mixing efficiency.2.Attach 100 μL sample loops to the MHQ device. Each MHQ time point requires 200 μL of CNBD solution (300 μM protein concentration) and 500 μL of cAMP (30 mM ligand concentration).Note: MHQ samples of the CNBD/cAMP system are prepared at a considerably lower volume than for the aging time calibration with MetMb/NaN3. This is because the subsequent PELDOR experiments will be performed at Q-band, which has an intrinsically higher concentration sensitivity than X-band.Optional: When connecting the sample loops, use a wrench to tighten (i.e., beyond finger-tight), as sample loops often eject under the high pressure formed upon switching the injection valve to the “inject” position.CRITICAL: Ensure that there are no leaks after replacing the sample loops. Perform several mock injections of PBS buffer into the protein and the ligand channel and switch the injection valve position from “load” to “inject”. Robust connections should tolerate pressures of over 2000 psi without leakage.3.Equilibrate the MHQ device in buffer (for details, see step 22 of the section “before you begin”).4.Switch on the MHQ device (for details, see step 24 of the section “before you begin).5.Start the software for controlling the cold-plate motor and the mixer-arm.a.Adjust the distance between the mixer and the cold-plate (for details, see steps 26a-c of the section “before you begin”).b.Check that the cold-plate can rotate freely (for details, see step 26e of the section “before you begin”).6.Enter a program code into the LinControl software with an optimized mixer-arm wait-time. Refer to steps 26d and 27 of the section “before you begin” for details.CRITICAL: Wear PPE (safety goggles or a face shield) for the next steps.7.Pre-cool isopentane to a temperature of ≤ −130°C in a flat-bottom metal Dewar flask equipped with a magnetic stirring rod to prevent freezing (see section “before you begin”, step 35).Note: Use a thermometer to monitor the temperature during the following steps.CRITICAL: The temperature of the isopentane bath must always remain ≤ −130°C to prevent sample thawing.8.Pre-cool the funnel for sample packing (see step 36 of the section “before you begin”) and the cold-plate (see step 37 of the section “before you begin”).9.Purge the protein and ligand Hamilton syringes, first with MilliQ H2O, followed by deuterated 1 × PBS buffer (see step 9a of the section “before you begin”).a.Draw 100 μL of the CNBD (300 μM) and the cAMP ligand (30 mM) into the syringes, taking care to remove air bubbles.b.Filter the samples before drawing them into the syringes to remove precipitates or other particulate matter that might clog the orifice.Alternatives: Separate any particulate matter by centrifugation (13,000 × g, 5 min, 4°C).c.Insert the syringes into the MHQ injection valves (in the “load” position).10.Acquire the MHQ sample (see step 41 of the section “before you begin”, or Table 6).11.Collect and pack the MHQ sample.a.Scrape the sample off the cold-plate walls (see step 41g of the section “before you begin”) and transfer the sample into the funnel (see step 42 and 45 of the section “before you begin”).b.Pack the sample in a 3 mm o.d. EPR tube (see step 45 of the section “before you begin”).12.Anneal the sample tube as described in step 53b of the section “before you begin” to remove N2(l) trapped in sample voids. Compress the sample with a packing rod, cryogenically cooled in N2(l). Troubleshooting 2.

Pulse dipolar EPR spectroscopy (PDS) is a technique to measure the distance between unpaired electrons in the range of 1.5–16 nm with Angstrom precision.22,25,26,27 The PDS toolbox encompasses several experiments,28 the most popular being PELDOR. PELDOR is typically performed on ensembles of biomolecules in frozen solution and is exclusively sensitive to unpaired electron spins, i.e., it is blind to the diamagnetic “background”. The long-range distance constraints provided by PELDOR are complementary to the atomic resolution achieved by X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM, but without necessitating crystallization or surface immobilization. Furthermore, PELDOR is virtually unrestricted with respect to the size of the biomolecule, facilitating the study of complex molecular machinery29,30,31 with the ribosome32 being the largest molecular complex studied by PELDOR, to date. Of note, the nitroxide spin labels most often used for PELDOR are comparatively small and structurally less perturbing than the sterically bulkier fluorophores used in FRET.33 In this purview, PELDOR has been extensively applied to proteins and nucleic acids, characterizing (i) conformational dynamics,34,35,36 (ii) domain rearrangements,37 (iii) binding equilibria,38,39,40,41 (iv) oligomerization,42,43 and (v) the kinetics of these processes.1,44,45,46

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions and media
steps.instruction: Make all reagents needed for expression, purification and spin‑labeling.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10 mL ampicillin stock (100 mg mL⁻¹) in filtered Milli‑Q water.
Prepare 10 mL IPTG stock (1 M) in filtered Milli‑Q water.
Prepare LB agar plates with 100 µg mL⁻¹ ampicillin (add 12 g agar per L LB).
Prepare 50 mL LB broth (10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 10 g NaCl per L, adjust to pH 7.0 with 200 µL 5 M NaOH) and autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min; store at 4 °C.
Prepare five 1 L batches of Terrific Broth (TB) in 2 L flasks, cover with foil and autoclave.
Prepare the following buffers (store at 4 °C unless noted):
1× PBS (1 L: 150 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl, 10 mM Na₂HPO₄, 1.8 mM KH₂PO₄, pH 7.4).
1 mL aliquots of 1 M DTT, store at –80 °C.
250 mL 1× PBS + 10 mM DTT + EDTA‑free protease inhibitor cocktail (add immediately before use).
Refolding buffer (500 mL: 7 mM Na₂HPO₄, 3 mM NaH₂PO₄, 150 mM NaCl, 500 mM L‑arginine, 10 mM EDTA, pH 7.4).
Denaturing buffer (500 mL: 7 mM Na₂HPO₄, 3 mM NaH₂PO₄, 150 mM NaCl, 6 M guanidine, pH 7.4).
MTSSL spin label: 25 µL aliquots of 100 mM MTSSL (26.44 mg mL⁻¹ in DMSO), store at –80 °C.
70 % (v/v) EtOH, 50 mL for cleaning the sonicator.

steps.title: Verify plasmid and prepare for transformation
steps.instruction: Check plasmid integrity and set up aseptic conditions before transforming cells.

substeps.instruction: Confirm plasmid sequence by Sanger sequencing and assess quality on a 1 % agarose gel (load 20 ng DNA).
Extract plasmid DNA with a miniprep kit.
Disinfect work surfaces with 70 % (v/v) EtOH, wear nitrile gloves and lab coat, work near a Bunsen burner, and minimise exposure to open air.

steps.title: Transform BL21(DE3) pLysE cells
steps.instruction: Introduce the verified plasmid into chemically‑competent BL21(DE3) pLysE cells.

substeps.instruction: Thaw 50 µL of competent cells on ice; add ~50 ng plasmid DNA.
Incubate on ice 30 min, heat‑shock at 42 °C for 45 s, return to ice 2 min.
Add 200 µL LB (room temperature) and incubate 37 °C, 800 rpm, 1 h.
Plate on LB‑ampicillin agar and incubate 16 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare starter culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate a single colony into LB‑ampicillin broth.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate 50 mL LB + 100 µg mL⁻¹ ampicillin in a 500 mL baffled flask.
Incubate 16 h at 37 °C, 180 rpm.

steps.title: Large‑scale expression
steps.instruction: Scale up culture, induce protein expression, and harvest cells.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate five 1 L TB flasks (each with 100 µg mL⁻¹ ampicillin) with starter culture; ensure OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.2 at inoculation.
Grow in a fermenter at 37 °C, 1 500 rpm, airflow 7 mL min⁻¹ until OD₆₀₀ = 2.5–3.0.
Reduce temperature to 20 °C and add IPTG to 0.8 mM final concentration.
Incubate 20 h at 20 °C, 1 500 rpm, 7 mL min⁻¹ airflow.
Harvest cells by centrifugation 6 000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant and store pellets at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare amylose resin
steps.instruction: Condition the amylose resin for affinity chromatography.

substeps.instruction: Decant resin into a 10 mL gravity column (0.2 mL g⁻¹ cell pellet).
Wash 3 × 10 mL Milli‑Q water to remove 20 % EtOH storage solution.
Wash 3 × 10 mL 0.1 % (v/v) SDS solution, then 5 × 10 mL 1× PBS (see step 1).
Store resin at 4 °C.

steps.title: Freeze‑dry refolding buffer
steps.instruction: Lyophilize 20 mL of refolding buffer and store at ambient temperature.

substeps.instruction: Seal the lyophilized buffer with Parafilm; keep at 18–25 °C.

steps.title: Cell lysis
steps.instruction: Thaw, resuspend, and sonicate cell pellets.

substeps.instruction: Thaw pellets; resuspend in 1× PBS (step 1) at 3 mL buffer per gram cell pellet.
Add DTT to 10 mM final and one protease‑inhibitor tablet per 50 mL buffer.
Sonicate on ice 4 min at 40 % of max amplitude; clean probe with 70 % EtOH before and after sonication.

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Remove debris by high‑speed centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge lysate 40 000 × g, 60 min, 4 °C; keep supernatant.

steps.title: Amylose affinity capture and washing
steps.instruction: Bind target protein to resin, wash, and exchange into denaturing buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add equilibrated amylose resin (0.2 mL g⁻¹ cell pellet) to supernatant; incubate 30 min, 4 °C with gentle agitation.
Centrifuge 4 000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend resin in supplemented 1× PBS (step 1c) at 2.5 mL per mL resin; repeat centrifugation. Perform this wash‑resuspend cycle five times to remove DTT and non‑specific proteins.
Exchange resin into denaturing buffer (step 1e) at 2.5 mL per mL resin; centrifuge 4 000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C and collect the supernatant.

steps.title: Spin‑labeling in denaturing buffer
steps.instruction: Label cysteines with MTSSL under denaturing conditions.

substeps.instruction: Add MTSSL to a 5‑fold molar excess over protein concentration.
Incubate 12–16 h at 4 °C protected from light (wrap tube in aluminium foil).

steps.title: Remove excess label and cAMP
steps.instruction: Wash labeled protein on a 30 kDa spin column.

substeps.instruction: Load the labeling mixture onto a 15 mL, 30 kDa MWCO spin column; centrifuge 4 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C.
Wash with 4 mL denaturing buffer (step 1e) at least three times, concentrating to ≈ 1 mL.
Confirm removal of cAMP by measuring A₂₆₀/A₂₈₀; a ratio ≈ 0.8 indicates cAMP‑free protein.

steps.title: Refold protein
steps.instruction: Dilute denatured, labeled protein into cold refolding buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 mL of the protein solution dropwise to 40 mL ice‑cold refolding buffer (step 1d) while stirring gently with a Pasteur pipette.
Centrifuge the mixture 4 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C using a 30 kDa spin column.
Repeat centrifugation as needed to reduce total volume to 2–4 mL.

steps.title: Size‑exclusion chromatography (SEC)
steps.instruction: Purify refolded protein on a Superdex 200 column and concentrate.

substeps.instruction: Attach a pre‑equilibrated HiLoad 16/60 Superdex 200 pg column to the ÄKTA system; equilibrate with two column volumes of 1× PBS (step 1a) (≈ 3–4 h).
Rinse the sample loop with two loop volumes of degassed Milli‑Q water, then two loop volumes of degassed 1× PBS (degassing performed by vacuum‑pumping into a Duran flask with magnetic stirring).
Draw the CNBD solution into a 5 mL syringe via a cannula (discard cannula after use) and load the loop (loop volume ≥ 2× sample volume, avoid bubbles).
Inject onto the column and elute with refolding buffer (step 1d).
Collect fractions; the monodisperse protein peak elutes at ≈ 84 mL.
Pool peak fractions and concentrate with a fresh 30 kDa spin column at 4 000 × g, 4 °C.
Adjust final protein concentration to 300 µM, aliquot 200 µL, snap‑freeze in liquid N₂, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Assess labeling efficiency (CW‑EPR)
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration, record a CW‑EPR spectrum, and calculate spin‑labeling efficiency.

substeps.instruction: Determine CNBD concentration by Nanodrop at 280 nm (ε₂₈₀ = 71 850 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹). Dilute an aliquot to ≈ 100 µM for CW‑EPR.
Place 15 µL of the ~100 µM solution in the lid of a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube; fill a 0.6 mm i.d. microcapillary with 10 µL of the same solution.
Seal the capillary with silicone paste, insert into a 4 mm o.d. X‑band EPR tube, and mount in the resonator of the EMXnano CW‑EPR spectrometer.

Tune the spectrometer (Xepr software): open tuning panel, switch to tune mode, click “Lock Search”, wait for “Operate” mode, verify Matching = 0 µA and Matching Fine ≈ 0 %; repeat if needed; ensure Operate, Levelled and Calibrated indicators are green.

Record a CW‑EPR spectrum at 298 K using parameters from Table 1 (10 scans, 1300 points, centre field 3445 G, attenuation 16 dB, sweep width 130 G, receiver gain 40 dB, conversion time 20.94 ms, time‑constant 20.48 ms, modulation amplitude 1 G).

Open the “Quantitative EPR” → “SpinCount” tab; define the whole spectrum as region, set baseline bars, click “Double Integration”, then “Calculate”. Enter inner capillary diameter = 0.6 mm, centre = 125 mm, length ≈ 25 mm. Record the spin concentration.
Calculate labeling efficiency using Equation 1: labeling % = [c(spins µM) / (n × c(protein µM))] × 100, where n = 2 (two cysteines). Values ≥ 75 % are recommended.

steps.title: Exchange buffer to D₂O
steps.instruction: Replace H₂O‑based refolding buffer with deuterated buffer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the CNBD sample in a 30 kDa spin column at 4 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; repeat until final volume ≈ 100 µL.
Add 400 µL deuterated refolding buffer (step 1d prepared in D₂O) and repeat the spin‑column exchange at least three times.
Adjust final protein concentration to ≈ 300 µM, aliquot 200 µL, snap‑freeze in liquid N₂, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare MHQ samples
steps.instruction: Centrifuge protein and ligand, set up MHQ device, and pack samples into EPR tubes.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge 200 µL of 300 µM CNBD and 500 µL of 30 mM cAMP at 13 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; keep on ice.
Optional: add 20 % (v/v) deuterated ethylene glycol to both solutions to improve phase‑memory time.
Attach 100 µL sample loops to the MHQ device (each time point needs 200 µL protein + 500 µL ligand). Tighten loops with a wrench; verify no leaks by mock injections of PBS at > 2000 psi.
Equilibrate the MHQ device in buffer (see “before you begin” step 22).
Switch on the MHQ device (see “before you begin” step 24).
Start LinControl software; set mixer‑arm wait‑time as described in steps 26d‑27 of “before you begin”. Wear safety goggles or face shield.
Pre‑cool isopentane to ≤ –130 °C in a flat‑bottom metal Dewar with magnetic stirring; monitor temperature with a thermometer.
Pre‑cool the sample‑packing funnel (step 36) and the cold‑plate (step 37).
Purge protein and ligand Hamilton syringes sequentially with Milli‑Q H₂O then deuterated 1× PBS (step 9a of “before you begin”).
Draw 100 µL of CNBD (300 µM) and 100 µL of cAMP (30 mM) into the syringes; filter or centrifuge (13 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C) to remove particulates.
Insert syringes into MHQ injection valves (position “load”).
Acquire the MHQ sample (see step 41 of “before you begin”).
Scrape the frozen film from the cold‑plate walls (step 41g) into the pre‑cooled funnel (step 42, 45).
Pack the slurry into a 3 mm o.d. EPR tube (step 45).
Anneal the packed tube as described in step 53b: compress with a cryogenically cooled packing rod in liquid N₂ to remove trapped N₂.

steps.title: Cool spectrometer cryostat
steps.instruction: Prepare the Q‑band spectrometer for PELDOR measurements.

substeps.instruction: Cool the cryostat to 50 K using liquid helium (see “before you begin” step 53c).
Mount the MHQ‑packed EPR tube; position the sample centre 38 mm from the bottom of the holder (ensures active resonator volume).
Do NOT submerge the entire tube; only the sample region should be inside the resonator.
Quickly (≤ 5–10 s) transfer the tube from the Dewar, shake to remove residual N₂, and insert into the spectrometer (set magnetic field to 0 G before moving).

steps.title: Over‑couple resonator and safety check
steps.instruction: Set up the resonator for pulsed experiments.

substeps.instruction: Perform the safety check to confirm protection gates are engaged.
Switch the TWT amplifier to “Operate” mode if protection gates are present.

steps.title: Record echo‑detected field‑swept (EDFS) spectrum
steps.instruction: Acquire a field‑swept Hahn‑echo spectrum to locate the resonance.

substeps.instruction: Set Center Field to the g ≈ 2.0 value (≈ 11980 G at 33.7 GHz).
Program the Hahn‑echo sequence (π/2 – τ – π – τ – echo) in the “+x” channel: π/2 = 12 ns, π = 24 ns, τ = 200 ns.
Set Acquisition Trigger: Position = 0 ns, Length = 4 ns.
Set Integrator Time Base = 1.0 ns, Shots per point = 10, Shot‑Repetition Time (SRT) = 2000 µs (typical start for nitroxides at 50 K, Q‑band).
Set Video Bandwidth = 20 MHz; start the pulse program and run, decreasing microwave attenuation until the echo amplitude maximises (≈ 3 dB attenuation gives π/2 = 12 ns, π = 24 ns).
If echo does not maximise, increase pulse lengths (e.g., π/2 = 16 ns, π = 32 ns) and retune the resonator.
Adjust Center Field by ±10 G to maximise echo; optimise Signal Phase so the real (green) channel is maximal and the imaginary (yellow) channel is near zero.
Set number of averages = 1; adjust Video Gain to avoid clipping.
Select X‑Axis Quantity = Magnetic Field; set Acquisition Trigger Position ≈ 790 ns, Length ≈ 120 ns to integrate the full echo.
Set Sweep Width = 400 G; set X‑Axis Size = 800 points (2 points per G).
Run acquisition, save the EDFS spectrum; acquire 3–5 scans if needed for sufficient SNR.

steps.title: Determine longitudinal relaxation (T₁) by inversion‑recovery
steps.instruction: Measure T₁ to optimise shot‑repetition time.

substeps.instruction: Set Center Field to the EDFS maximum.
Open PulseSPEL editor; load “InvRec_ESE.exp” and “descrRelaxation.def”.
Update variable definitions as in Table 8 (e.g., p0 = 12 ns, p1 = 24 ns, p2 ≈ 24 ns, d0, d1, d2, etc.).
Compile, validate, and run the inversion‑recovery sequence (πinv – T – π/2 – τ – π – τ – echo).
Monitor the inverted Hahn echo; adjust d0 so the acquisition trigger aligns with the echo maximum.
Record the echo amplitude versus T; determine the time at which the echo reaches 80 % of the plateau – set this as the new SRT for subsequent experiments.

steps.title: Measure phase‑memory time (T_M) by two‑pulse ESEEM
steps.instruction: Obtain T_M to set the dipolar evolution time for PELDOR.

substeps.instruction: Set Center Field to the EDFS maximum.
Load “2p_ESEEM.exp” and “descrESEEM.def” in PulseSPEL.
Update variables (Table 10): p0 = 12 ns, p1 = 24 ns, d0, d1 (initial τ), d30 (τ increment), h = 10, n = 1, SRT as determined above.
Compile and validate; select “Acquisition Mode: Run from PulseSPEL” and “2P ESE Setup”.
Set Acquisition Trigger to the echo maximum; optimise Signal Phase for maximal real component.
Set number of averages = 1; adjust Video Gain to avoid clipping.
Record the two‑pulse ESEEM trace (e.g., dim2 = 1024 points, time‑step = 8 ns → ≈ 8 µs total).
Determine the τ at which the echo decays to ≈ 5 % of its initial intensity; note this τ (typically 1–2 µs) as a starting point for the PELDOR dipolar evolution time τ₂.

steps.title: Set up PELDOR experiment (4‑pulse DEER)
steps.instruction: Load the DEER program, define pulse lengths, and optimise pump/probe parameters.

substeps.instruction: Load the 4‑pulse DEER PulseSPEL program and its variable definition file.
Set probe π/2‑pulse (p0) and π‑pulse (p1) to the values optimised in step 17 (12 ns and 24 ns).
Set τ₁ (d1) to the τ value giving the global maximum in the two‑pulse ESEEM trace (e.g., 232 ns).
Set τ₂ (d2) initially to the value used in step 18 (the dipolar evolution time).
Set d3 (spectrometer dead time) = 100 ns.
Set integration gate width (pg) to the longest pulse in the sequence (24 ns).
Set acquisition trigger offset (d0) so the gate is centred on the echo maximum (typically ≈ 432 ns).
Set d30 (increment of dipolar evolution) according to Nyquist criteria (see Table 11).
Set nuclear‑modulation averaging: m = 8, d31 = 16 ns (for deuterated samples).
Set number of scans (n) to a high value (e.g., 10 000) and number of points (dim5) using Equation 23: dim5 = (d1 + d2 – 2 d3)/d30.
Select phase‑cycling option “2‑step”.

steps.title: Optimise ELDOR pump frequency and attenuation
steps.instruction: Find the pump frequency (ν_pump) and set appropriate attenuation.

substeps.instruction: In the “Microwave” tab, note the current microwave frequency (≈ 33.7 GHz) – this is ν_pump.
Select “3P ELDOR Setup”; run and observe the Hahn echo.
Decrease “ELDOR Attenuation” stepwise to 0 dB; adjust d0 so the acquisition trigger aligns with the echo maximum (typically d0 = 432 ns).

steps.title: Determine optimal pump‑pulse length (π_pump)
steps.instruction: Run a transient nutation experiment to set the pump pulse for maximal inversion.

substeps.instruction: Select “3P ELDOR Nutation”; run and record the nutation trace.
Save the trace, read off the pump‑pulse length that gives maximal echo inversion (typically 12–18 ns).
Set this value as p2 (π_pump) in the DEER PulseSPEL program.

steps.title: Switch to probe frequency (ν_probe)
steps.instruction: Offset the microwave frequency to obtain the probe frequency.

substeps.instruction: Set Attenuation = 60 dB and ELDOR Attenuation = 30 dB.
Switch TWT to “Standby”; wait for cathode voltage to drop to 0 V.
In “Bridge Configuration”, set microwave bridge to CW mode.
Open “Microwave Bridge Tuning”; lower the frequency by Δν ≈ –80 to –100 MHz (e.g., set to 33.6 GHz) to obtain ν_probe.
Activate the FCL option to stabilise the frequency.

steps.title: Optimise Hahn echo at probe frequency
steps.instruction: Fine‑tune the resonator and pulse parameters for ν_probe.

substeps.instruction: Switch back to pulse mode; fine‑adjust probe frequency to maximise echo.
Perform safety check and set TWT to “Operate”.
Set acquisition trigger delay d0 = 360 ns.
Select “2P ESE Setup” with phase‑cycling “+ none”; run and adjust Attenuation and ELDOR Attenuation to 0 dB, adjust Video Gain to avoid clipping.
Fine‑adjust “+ Amplitude” slider (≈ 72 % of max) to maximise the real echo; set “+ Phase” so the real echo is negative‑going.

Repeat with “– none” phase cycling; adjust “– Amplitude” (≈ 72 %) and “– Phase” so the real echo is positive‑going; ensure both traces have comparable absolute amplitudes and the imaginary channel averages to zero.

steps.title: Choose dipolar evolution time τ₂
steps.instruction: Select τ₂ that resolves the expected distance distribution.

substeps.instruction: Use the τ₂ value from step 18 as a starting point.
If needed, calculate the dipolar period t_Dip from Equation 20/21 and ensure τ₂ ≥ 1.5 × t_Dip (see Equation 22).
Adjust τ₂ in the PulseSPEL variable d2 accordingly.

steps.title: Run 4‑pulse DEER (PELDOR) acquisition
steps.instruction: Collect the dipolar trace with the parameters defined in Table 11.

substeps.instruction: Select “4P DEER Setup”, phase‑cycling “2‑step”, and press “Run”.
Start the pulse tables, run SpecJet, and observe the refocused echo (RE).
Set number of transient averages = 1; adjust Video Gain to avoid clipping.
Increase number of averages (e.g., 100–1000) to reach SNR > 20; run the experiment.
Set integration gate width (pg) to 24 ns; centre the gate on the echo maximum by adjusting d0.
Acquire the dipolar trace; stop when SNR is satisfactory (preferably > 20).
Save the dataset (both real and imaginary parts) to disk.

steps.title: Shut down spectrometer and retrieve sample
steps.instruction: Safely end the measurement and remove the sample.

substeps.instruction: Drag all MPFU channel sliders to zero.
Set Attenuation = 60 dB, ELDOR Attenuation = 30 dB, and switch TWT to Standby.
Switch microwave bridge to CW mode, set frequency to 33.7 GHz, and set bridge to Standby.
Turn off the membrane pump and wait for pressure to return to ambient.
Remove the sample rod from the cryostat; transfer the tube quickly into a Dewar filled with liquid N₂.

steps.title: Process PELDOR data
steps.instruction: Analyse the dipolar trace using DeerAnalysis (or alternatives).

substeps.instruction: Open DeerAnalysis; import the background‑corrected dipolar trace.
Perform background correction, Tikhonov regularisation, and obtain the distance distribution P(r).
Optional: use ComparativeDeerAnalyzer (CDA) for one‑step background correction and distance extraction.

steps.title: Deconvolute MHQ dipolar trace
steps.instruction: Determine apo‑ and holo‑state populations by linear combination fitting.

substeps.instruction: Open the deconvolver GUI; enable “force a + b = 1”, “save ASCII files”, “save PNG files”, and “generate report”.
Select the ASCII files for apo‑state, holo‑state, and MHQ dipolar traces; press “RUN”.
The GUI scales holo‑ and MHQ‑traces to the apo‑trace modulation depth (Equation 26).
Fit a first‑order polynomial to the residual; ensure intercept and slope ≈ 0 (good fit).
Record the coefficients a (apo fraction) and b (holo fraction) for kinetic analysis.
Tabulate the coefficients for subsequent kinetic modelling.
